prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Pasadena, Texas, and has neck and back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1275; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my full name on a recording, but you can use the claim reference.
Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where you were when the accident happened?
A: I was driving on a city street in Pasadena, Texas, heading toward a shopping center. Traffic was light.
Q: What happened next?
A: The other car came over into my lane. We were going slow, maybe fifteen miles an hour, but it was a head-on hit. My airbag didn't deploy.
Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?
A: Yes, I was.
Q: Did you hit your head or lose consciousness?
A: No, I didn't black out. I just got jolted forward and then pushed back against the seat.
Q: Did you get out of the vehicle at the scene?
A: I got out, but my neck and lower back were already stiff. I sat on the curb for a while until the police arrived.
Q: Have you sought medical treatment since the accident?
A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic the same day. They diagnosed a neck strain and a back strain. I've been doing physical therapy twice a week since then.
Q: Are you currently having any pain or limitations?
A: Yes. Turning my head to the left hurts, and I can't sit for long periods without my lower back aching. I've had to miss a few days of work.
Q: Thank you. Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I'm still going to physical therapy and I'll send over my records as soon as I get them.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
